F1: matchFiles` sorts filenames, so the "last filename" rule picks by slug rather than by date, and a re-review with an earlier-sorting slug can never clear a FAIL.
F2: parseFrontmatter` returns `{found:false}` on every failure and flattens nested keys with last-wins, so it can't name the parse failure as the doc requires, and a nested `verdict`/`status` can overwrite the top-level value.
F3: the doc says "four slice-level transitions," but the config lists three slice-level transitions plus `pre-slice-plan`, and only `pre-advance` has an insertion point and statuses.
F4: validateValue` runs only in `set()` and `get()` casts raw TOML without checking it, so hand-edited values bypass the "fail-fast via `validate`" principle the doc relies on.
F5: review_unknown_as` is shown as `"fail"`, `"concern"` and a "pending" behavior, while the threshold uses `"concerns"`, and no allowed-value set is ever defined.
F6: the named status values are exposed through `SliceStatus` in `getStatus`, so the design goal can be met; the rest is design preference.
F7: the doc already says read and parse failures map to UNKNOWN with an explicit rationale, so the broad catch is an implementation concern, not a doc defect.
F8: the navigator already receives `projectPath` and can build its own config reader, so no per-surface work is forced; the injection style is an implementation choice.
F9: 180 defines CWD→project resolution and places configuration at the shared project level; it introduces no worktree-scoped config resolution chain.
F10: asking for a shared filename parser is a refactoring preference; the new rule simply mirrors the detector's existing prefix matching.
F11: numeric enforcement is explicitly deferred, so who owns the future threshold is scope opinion, not a v1 defect.
F12: warning on freshly completed or historical slices without a review is the opt-in signal the rule is meant to give; grandfathering is a policy preference.
F13: this is an opinion about scope and complexity, not a defect.
F14: note 001 itself lists UNKNOWN/missing handling as a decision the architecture must make, and calls the key names tentative.
